note: Seed text written for the demo; not yet reviewed by SWS (OT-04). Keyed for now by WHM issue type; map to Siteimprove rule or policy IDs once known.

types.title: Images are missing text descriptions
types.what: Some images have no alternative text, so people using screen readers don’t know what the image shows.
types.why: Text descriptions are required at WCAG level A. Missing ones are among the most common barriers for blind visitors.
types.todo: Edit each image listed below and add a short description of what it shows. Decorative images can be marked as decorative instead.

types.title: Link text doesn’t say where the link goes
types.what: Links use wording like “click here” or “read more” that only makes sense with the text around it.
types.why: People who move through a page by its links hear the link text on its own.
types.todo: Rewrite each link so its words name the destination, for example “Read the accessibility guide.”

types.title: Links lead to pages that don’t exist
types.what: These links point to pages that return a “not found” error.
types.why: Broken links send visitors to a dead end and make the site look out of date.
types.todo: Update each link to the right address, or remove it if the page is gone for good.

types.title: PDFs may not work with screen readers
types.what: These PDFs aren’t tagged, so their structure can’t be read by assistive technology.
types.why: Untagged PDFs can be unreadable for screen reader users.
types.todo: Replace the PDF with a web page where possible, or re-export it as a tagged PDF.

types.title: Some text is too light to read easily
types.what: A few text styles don’t have enough contrast against their background.
types.why: Low contrast makes text hard to read for many visitors, especially on phones outdoors.
types.todo: No action needed from you. This comes from the site template, and SWS is handling it.

types.title: Pages not updated in over a year
types.what: These pages haven’t changed in more than 12 months. (In this demo the age check is simulated; the data source is still being chosen.)
types.why: Out-of-date content is the most common reason site owners make changes. Some pages are fine as they are, such as a page updated once a year.
types.todo: Check each page. Update it, or choose “They’re still correct” if it doesn’t need a change.

types.title: Pages share the same title
types.what: Several pages use the same page title.
types.why: In search results, visitors can’t tell these pages apart.
types.todo: Give each page a title that describes what is on it.

types.title: Pages are missing a search description
types.what: These pages have no summary for search engines to show.
types.why: Without one, search engines pick text from the page, which may not help visitors decide to click.
types.todo: Add a one- or two-sentence summary in each page’s search description field.

types.title: Uses an outdated office name
types.what: These pages use a name that Stanford has replaced.
types.why: A Stanford content policy checks for retired names so messages stay consistent across sites.
types.todo: Replace the old name with the current one on each page.
